ai.intro: LordOS's selection of AI tools: agents that code with you, editors, and engines that run models and turn speech into text on this computer. Apps whose maker has a signed repository come from it, with the maker's key pinned by LordOS; the others come from LordOS's signed repository, built by LordOS from verified sources or copied after checking the maker's signature.

ai.sourceIntro: {name} comes from {vendor}'s own repository. Installing it adds that repository to this computer, with {vendor}'s signing key that LordOS's catalog pins: from then on its updates come from {vendor}, checked with that key, over HTTPS.
ai.title: Artificial Intelligence
commercial.drivers: Drivers for your graphics card are offered in For this computer when LordOS finds the card.
commercial.intro: Free-of-charge apps whose source code isn't public: browsers, music, games and drivers from their makers. LordOS checks that each one comes from its maker, signed with the key LordOS pins, but can't review or fix what they do; they get the same firewall and permissions as any other Linux app.
remote.intro: Apps for reaching this computer from another one, from makers outside LordOS. They aren't LordOS's Remote Desktop on port 5673: only one of the two can use a session at a time, and each person who comes in is accepted at the computer. LordOS checks that each one comes from its maker, but can't review or fix what they do.
suites.intro: Open source apps and suites from other projects that we think are worth having. Each one comes from its maker: from the maker's signed repository, with the key LordOS pins, or from the maker's own package, which LordOS keeps with a pinned checksum. A suite's launcher may then download its apps from its maker. LordOS doesn't review or fix what they do; they get the same firewall and permissions as any other Linux app.

suggest.nvidiaDriver.detail: Right now it uses nouveau, the free driver included with LordOS. The vendor's driver ({packages}) usually gives better 3D performance and power management.
suggest.nvidiaDriver.note.nouveau: Until you install it, the free nouveau driver stays in use; removing the package goes back to it.
suggest.nvidiaDriver.note.older: Cards older than about 2014 aren't supported by this driver version; keep the free driver on them. The LordOS desktop hasn't been tested with this driver yet.
suggest.nvidiaDriver.note.secureBoot: The driver is built for your kernel on this computer (DKMS) and again after every kernel update. With Secure Boot on, you have to enroll its signing key at the next restart, or the driver won't load.

suggest.nvidiaDriver.unavailable: The vendor's driver needs Debian's contrib and non-free components, and they aren't both enabled in this computer's package sources. The free driver, nouveau, keeps working.
